title: React Forms: Events, Inputs, Actions and Validation
summary: Quick revision of React synthetic events, controlled vs uncontrolled inputs, form submission with preventDefault, React 19 form actions, useActionState and validation patterns.

chapters.title: Synthetic Events and the Mental Model
points: SyntheticEvent is React's cross-browser wrapper around the native event; the native event is at e.nativeEvent
Handlers are camelCase props receiving a function reference: onClick={handleClick}, not onClick={handleClick()}
React 17+ attaches listeners at the root container, not on document, and no longer pools events, so async access to e is safe
e.target is the element that fired the event, e.currentTarget is the element the handler is attached to
onChange in React fires on every keystroke (like native input), unlike native change which fires on blur

chapters.title: Controlled vs Uncontrolled Inputs
points: Controlled: value comes from state and onChange updates it, so React is the single source of truth: <input value={name} onChange={e => setName(e.target.value)} />
Uncontrolled: DOM holds the value; read it via a ref (ref.current.value) or FormData on submit; seed with defaultValue/defaultChecked
Checkbox uses checked and e.target.checked; select uses value on <select>; file input is always uncontrolled
Comparison: controlled gives instant validation, conditional disabling and input formatting but re-renders per keystroke; uncontrolled is simpler and cheaper for submit-only forms
Gotcha: value without onChange makes a read-only field with a warning; switching value from undefined to a string flips uncontrolled to controlled, so initialise state with ''

chapters.title: Form Submission and preventDefault
points: onSubmit goes on <form>, not on the button; Enter in a field and a click on a submit button both trigger it
e.preventDefault() stops the browser's full-page navigation/reload so React handles the submit itself
Read all fields without state: const data = new FormData(e.currentTarget); Object.fromEntries(data) or data.get('email')
Fields need a name attribute to appear in FormData; <button> defaults to type="submit", so use type="button" for non-submitting buttons
Example: function onSubmit(e){ e.preventDefault(); const fd = new FormData(e.currentTarget); save(Object.fromEntries(fd)); }

chapters.title: Form Actions in React 19
points: Pass a function to <form action={fn}> instead of a URL; React calls fn(formData) on submit and auto-prevents default
Actions run inside a transition, so they can be async and the UI stays responsive; uncontrolled uncontrolled fields reset automatically after a successful action
useFormStatus() from react-dom returns { pending, data, method, action } and must be called in a child component rendered inside the <form>, not in the form's own component
formAction prop on <button> overrides the form's action per button, e.g. Save draft vs Publish
Comparison with onSubmit: action gives FormData, automatic reset and pending state with no preventDefault; onSubmit is still right for controlled forms and custom client-side flow
Server Functions marked 'use server' can be passed as action and work before hydration (progressive enhancement)

chapters.title: useActionState and Validation Patterns
points: const [state, formAction, isPending] = useActionState(fn, initialState) where fn is (prevState, formData) => newState
Return validation errors as state, not exceptions: return { errors: { email: 'Required' }, values }; render state.errors next to each field
Echo submitted values back and use defaultValue={state.values?.email} because React 19 resets uncontrolled fields after the action
Validate on the server (or in the action) as the source of truth; client checks are only UX. Schema libraries like Zod: schema.safeParse(Object.fromEntries(formData))
Pattern timing: validate on submit first, then on blur for touched fields, and on change only after the first error to avoid noisy errors
Use isPending to disable the submit button; use aria-invalid and aria-describedby on fields so errors are announced

chapters.title: React Forms Cheat Sheet
points: Events: onChange per keystroke, e.target vs e.currentTarget, nativeEvent for the raw event, pass handler not handler()
Controlled = value + onChange; uncontrolled = defaultValue + ref/FormData; init state with '' not undefined
Classic submit: onSubmit + e.preventDefault() + new FormData(e.currentTarget); inputs need name
React 19: <form action={fn}> gets FormData, auto-resets uncontrolled fields, runs in a transition
useFormStatus in a child of the form; useActionState(fn, init) returns [state, formAction, isPending]
Validation: server is the truth, return errors as state, echo values back, disable on isPending
